name: MST in Modulo Graph
description: You are given a complete graph with $$$n$$$ vertices, where the $$$i$$$-th vertex has a weight $$$p_i$$$. The weight of the edge connecting vertex $$$x$$$ and vertex $$$y$$$ is equal to $$$\operatorname{max}(p_x, p_y) \bmod \operatorname{min}(p_x, p_y)$$$. Find the smallest total weight of a set of $$$n - 1$$$ edges that connect all $$$n$$$ vertices in this graph.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$). The next line of each test contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$ ($$$1 \le p_i \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$). The sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$. The sum of $$$\max(p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_n)$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer — the weight of the minimum spanning tree.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2081D — MST in Modulo Graph [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
